---
title: "Polynomial extrema counts"
---


Consider the [polynomial function](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polynomial#Definition) with leading coefficient $a$ and degree $n$.

$$y=ax^n+bx^{n-1}+\cdots+px^2+qx+r$$

where coefficient $b$, $p$, $q$, and $r$ are real-number constants (called coefficients). There are other coefficients as well, with the number of coefficients depending on the degree of the polynomial. It should be mentioned that $n$ is a positive integer and $a$ is nonzero.

As the degree of the polynomial increases, so does the maximum amount of extrema.

The parity (even or odd) of $n$, along with the sign (positive or negative) of $a$, determines the end behavior on the left and right.


| $n$ | sign of $a$ | number of extrema | left end | right end |
|:---:|:-----:|:---------:|:-------------:|:-------------:|
| 2   | $a>0$ | 1         | up  | up  |
| 2   | $a<0$ | 1         | down | down | 
| 3   | $a>0$ | 0 or 2    | down | up  | 
| 3   | $a<0$ | 0 or 2    | up | down |
| 4   | $a>0$ | 1 or 3    | up | up  | 
| 4   | $a<0$ | 1 or 3    | down | down |
| 5   | $a>0$ | 0 or 2 or 4    | down | up  | 
| 5   | $a<0$ | 0 or 2 or 4   | up | down |
| 6   | $a>0$ | 1 or 3 or 5   | up | up  | 
| 6   | $a<0$ | 1 or 3 or 5   | down | down |
